wn.name: WaterCraft
wn.numbers: Everything here is a calculation aid. A water engineer checks every result; the numbers are not a certificate or a stamped design.
wn.privacy: Your network stays in this project and on this computer. Nothing is sent anywhere.
wn.stopped: Stopped early: the list is only what was done.
wn.more: {n} more rows are in the CSV.
wn.err.nonet: There is no water network in this project yet. Draw junctions, a reservoir and pipes with the Water mains tools first.
wn.err.noloads: Paste at least one load line first.
wn.err.trace_node: Pick the reservoir or tank the trace starts from.
wn.err.not_configured: WaterCraft could not reach the water solver. Reload the page.
wn.dem.help: One customer per line: id, x, y, kind, amount. Kind is one of {kinds}, or flow for a typed flow. Amount is units (homes), area (acres, or hectares in metric) or a flow. Each goes to the nearest junction.
wn.dem.share: Share a load between junctions within about 300 ft (90 m)
wn.pat.keep: Keep the pattern as it is
wn.dem.starting: The use per home or per acre is a starting value, not a standard. Replace it with your utility's own design figures before you trust a result.
wn.dem.result: {total} {u} in total on {n} junctions; {bad} lines could not be placed.
wn.dem.applied: Demands written to the water mains. Undo takes them back.
wn.fire.help: For each hydrant (or every junction when none is marked): the flow it can give while the pressure holds the residual, found with the same solver as the Water mains window.
wn.fire.mult: Demand multiplier (1 = the demand as drawn; use your peak-day factor)
wn.limit.system: the lowest point in the system
wn.crit.help: Takes each main out of service in turn and solves again: how much demand is cut off, and which junctions fall under the minimum pressure. With valves placed on the pipes you can take out a whole valved section.
wn.crit.segment: one valved section at a time
wn.crit.result: {n} outages tried; {cut} cut some customers off.
wn.q.help: Follows water through the 24-hour run: how old it is, how much chlorine is left, or where it came from. Uses the demand pattern and tank levels of the Water mains.
wn.q.result: {n} junctions outside the limits you set.
wn.q.limits: First-order decay only, a tank is one mixed volume, no booster stations yet. Run long enough for the pattern to repeat before you read the last day.
